wave_3_input_risks.title: Terminal Core Reviewer Contract
wave_3_input_risks.goal: Redesign the terminal Phase 2 reviewer contract so the final core-review pass must close every surviving packet as TP or FP, instead of permitting REVIEW ambiguity to survive behind assessment=keep or needs_more_evidence.
wave_3_input_risks.status_summary: Wave 13 is complete with non-heavy validation. Phase 2 now has a first-class terminal_core reviewer mode with a dedicated prompt, system prompt, input builder path, and output schema. The terminal round only receives unresolved packets, forbids needs_more_evidence, rejects keep+REVIEW ambiguity, and drives reviewer-authored TP/FP closure into the terminal-closure helper. The old deterministic unresolved->FP path now survives only as a controlled fallback when the terminal reviewer round fails structurally.
design_objectives: The final core-review authority must not be able to preserve a REVIEW verdict through assessment=keep.
needs_more_evidence is valid only in intermediate rounds, not in the terminal reviewer round.
The terminal reviewer round must remain packet-local, evidence-first, and bounded rather than becoming a new broad explorer pass.
When exploitability still cannot be proved after bounded tracing, the packet must close as FP with explicit reopen conditions.

wave_3_input_risks.title: Cluster Authority Realignment
wave_3_input_risks.goal: Demote cluster synth/challenge from 'final ambiguity carrier' to a bounded advisory/refutation layer that either supports a closure decision or returns packets to a dedicated closure path, rather than letting open questions survive into the canonical artifact.
wave_3_input_risks.status_summary: Wave 14 is complete with non-heavy validation. Cluster synthesis/challenge now treat remaining ambiguity as either advisory-only metadata or explicit closure-routing packets. The cluster output contract gained closure_packets, materializers now normalize closure routing counts, and consensus no longer degrades trust simply because advisory open_questions or missing_evidence exist. Instead, a cluster only remains unresolved when its outputs are structurally missing or when a needs_followup/mixed result fails to emit the required closure-routing packet.
design_objectives: Cluster outputs should remain bounded to evidence-pack reasoning and refutation, not become a second ambiguous review loop.
Cluster ambiguity should be routable back into a closure packet, not remain a blocker embedded in consensus.
A cluster may challenge or split a hypothesis, but it should not preserve REVIEW as a terminal artifact state.

wave_3_input_risks.title: Consensus Trust Policy Realignment
wave_3_input_risks.goal: Redefine Phase 2 trust so success means 'structurally valid and fully closed for downstream use', while degraded_success is reserved for true structural/provenance/runtime defects rather than advisory uncertainty that should already have been closed earlier.
wave_3_input_risks.status_summary: Wave 15 is complete with non-heavy validation. Advisory cluster notes remain visible in metadata, but they do not downgrade trust by themselves. artifact_freshness and run-phase2 trust summarization now also treat trust_state=success as downstream-safe only when closure_complete is not false.
design_objectives: trust_state=success should mean downstream-safe canonical Phase 2, not merely a file that exists.
degraded_success should only represent structural or provenance issues, not advisory uncertainty that should have been closed in earlier waves.
Phase 2 admission to Phase 3 should remain fail-closed, but on the correct signals.

wave_plan.title: Cost-Aware Provider Strategy And Selective Claude Escalation
wave_plan.goal: Keep Codex as the default execution baseline while only invoking Claude when Phase 1 and Phase 2 evidence indicate high-value exploit potential or high-value ambiguity.
wave_plan.status_summary: Wave 6 is implemented and validated without a heavy rerun. The policy must distinguish pre-Phase-2 potential from post-worker evidence quality.
Decision logs must explain both why Claude was used and why it was not used.

pre_phase2_tiers.intent: Use Claude only for narrow contradiction and ambiguity-heavy stages once Phase 1 indicates likely reportable surface.

pre_phase2_tiers.label: claude_escalated_high_value_target
pre_phase2_tiers.intent: Spend Claude only when both surface and business context imply a realistic high-impact finding set.
default_conditions: A2 conditions plus threat_context.priority_vulns intersects high-impact families
or deep-extended with unauth_ep and sql_sinks or coverage_gaps both present
or threat_context suggests account_takeover, privilege_escalation, auth_bypass, arbitrary_file_upload, file_deletion, ssrf, local_file_inclusion, or remote_file_inclusion

reviewer_core reports missed_findings > 0 on high-impact families
forced exploration or cluster stages leave unresolved open questions or missing evidence on a potentially reportable path
stored or second-order patterns exist with real storage keys or plausible persistence paths
non_goals: Do not use Claude as the default worker for all plugins.
Do not spend Claude on low-signal quick-triage runs.
Do not use provider diversity as a substitute for deterministic postprocess, cluster consensus, or trust gating.

design_objectives: Failure artifacts should say what actually happened at runtime, not use leftover names from older control-plane assumptions.

Console/log wording should reduce operator ambiguity without flooding inline output.
Chunked runs should emit a concise summary artifact so post-run triage does not require manual log stitching.
